clue.text: A table constructed to hold fourth case

indicators.note: something constructed is assembled afresh, so these letters are put together in a new order
to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
IV is the Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture is built to accommodate a fourth item, perhaps a fourth leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fourth' looks like a word to keep, but it is the Roman numeral for four.
explanation.definitionFit: The ablative is a grammatical case in Latin, often listed fifth or sixth among the noun cases.

clue.text: Police in corrupt state giving conclusive trial

indicators.note: something corrupt is debased and twisted, so these letters are disordered
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Police investigating a corrupt state put it to a decisive trial.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid test, from testing gold with nitric acid, is a decisive proof of real worth.

clue.text: Free braille translation

indicators.note: a translation renders words in a new form, so these letters are recast in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone offers to put text into braille at no charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like 'no charge' but means loose, as in a free translation.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean loose or not literal, as in a liberal translation, and also generous or unrestricted.

clue.text: End of story read out

indicators.note: reading out means speaking the words, so we go by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: a tale is a story; the spelling changes but the sound stays

explanation.surface: Someone reaches the end of a story being read aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail is the hindmost end of an animal or object, so the end of something.

clue.text: Potentially successful sailor breaking rank

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so the sailor goes within the other word

blocks.note: rank as an adjective means foul or vile
AB is an able seaman, an ordinary sailor

explanation.surface: A promising sailor breaks ranks on parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' reads as a line of soldiers, but it is the adjective meaning foul.
explanation.definitionFit: A viable plan is workable and capable of succeeding, so it may well succeed.

clue.text: Goodness close to Lenin's heart for left-winger

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letter is kept

blocks.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'goodness!'
by means near or beside
the central letter of the five-letter name

explanation.surface: A left-wing politician holds something dear, close to Lenin's own heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Corbyn led the UK Labour Party from 2015 to 2020 and sits firmly on its left wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Corbyn is a famous example of a British socialist politician from the left of Labour.

clue.text: Drinks emporium formerly infested with very loud insects

indicators.note: pests that infest something get inside it, so the other pieces go within

blocks.note: once means formerly
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud
lice are small parasitic insects

explanation.surface: A liquor shop used to be overrun by noisy bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: An off-licence is a British shop licensed to sell alcohol to drink off the premises.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-licence specialises in selling wine, beer and spirits, so it is a shop for drinks.

clue.text: Crazy to proscribe Scottish Labour leader

blocks.note: to proscribe is to forbid or ban
Anas Sarwar leads Scottish Labour

explanation.surface: It would be mad to outlaw the leader of Scottish Labour.
explanation.walkthrough: The leader is given by his first name, not by an initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Going bananas is informal slang for going mad, so bananas means crazy.

clue.text: New European editor repeatedly called for

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
E is the abbreviation for European
ED is the abbreviation for editor, here twice over

explanation.surface: A new European editor keeps being summoned.
explanation.definitionFit: When a situation calls for something, it requires it, so called for means required.

clue.text: Bible book in which Gabriel featured prominently

blocks.note: first meaning: the first book of the Old Testament
second meaning: the rock band fronted by singer Peter Gabriel

explanation.walkthrough: The angel Gabriel suggests scripture, but the angel appears in Luke, not here; this Gabriel is the rock singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis opens the Bible, and Genesis was the 1970s progressive rock group with Peter Gabriel as frontman.

clue.text: Time wasted securing building material, short by one tile

indicators.note: something wasted is ruined or broken up, so these letters are scrambled
falling short means the word loses its final letter
to secure something is to hold it fast, so the outer letters wrap around the rest

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a brick is a basic building material
a means one, as in 'a dog'

explanation.surface: Someone wastes time fetching building supplies and ends up one tile short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' just places the A beside the shortened material. 'Tile' reads as a noun counted in the surface, but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbricate is to lay things overlapping in rows, the way roof tiles or fish scales are arranged.

clue.text: Church on marshland boundary

indicators.note: in an across clue, a thing placed on another comes after it, so the church piece goes second

blocks.note: a fen is low, marshy land, as in East Anglia
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church is built on the edge of marshland.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence is a barrier that marks the edge or limit of a property, which is a boundary.

clue.text: Make an effort to accommodate old right-winger

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room inside, so the effort word holds the other piece

blocks.note: to try is to make an effort
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone strives to make room for an elderly conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party, which sits on the political right.

clue.text: Loyalty for one entering partnership

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so this piece sits within the other

blocks.note: an alliance is a partnership or union
e.g. means 'for example', so 'for one' signals it

explanation.surface: Loyalty is what one brings when joining a partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegiance is faithful commitment to a person, cause or country, a direct synonym of loyalty.

clue.text: Balti curry transported over for independent charitable organisation

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so one letter swaps out for another
transported means carried off and moved about, so these letters shift into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; a balti is a curry cooked in a metal dish
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
I is the abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: A takeaway curry is delivered to a self-sufficient charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotary clubs are local branches of Rotary International, a service body that raises money for good causes.

clue.text: Beauty parlour with built-in love lounge

indicators.note: something built in is fitted inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a beauty salon
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A beauty parlour has a romantic lounge built into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' looks romantic but is the zero of tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon is a public room for relaxing, especially the more comfortable lounge bar of a British pub.

clue.text: Pluralistic papers about poetry

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the papers word is read backwards

blocks.note: ID is identification, one's papers
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Newspapers run articles on poetry from many different viewpoints.
explanation.definitionFit: A pluralistic society or outlook embraces many kinds, so it is varied and mixed in character.

clue.text: Boffin's formula for e?

blocks.note: surface reading: a scientist's equation for the mathematical constant e
setter's reading: the letter e is what heads one breakfast food word, so the formula is that food's head

explanation.walkthrough: The mathematical constant e is a red herring; e is the first letter of a word for something laid by hens, and that is the 'formula'.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffin is British slang for a scientist or brainy expert, as is the informal word for an intellectual.

clue.text: Vegetables are cut up to be put on plates

indicators.note: cutting trims the end off, so the word loses its last letter
in a down clue, up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
dishes are plates

explanation.surface: Vegetables get chopped before they are served on plates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut up' reads as chopping, but it is two separate instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Radishes are crisp red root vegetables, often eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Foreign saint sounded English

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for saint
a bell that sounded rang
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A foreign holy man turns out to sound English.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange in its older sense means alien or from elsewhere, as in 'a stranger in a strange land'.

clue.text: The man wearing fancy belt and digital shield

indicators.note: someone wearing a belt is inside it, so the man sits within the other letters
fancy means elaborate or ornamented, so these letters are rearranged decoratively

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
him refers to the man

explanation.surface: A man dons a fancy belt and a hi-tech shield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests computers, but it means relating to fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: A thimble is a cap worn on the fingertip in sewing to protect it from the needle.

clue.text: Amateur caught by a secret service plant

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for amateur
c is cricket scorecard shorthand for caught
taken as written
the CIA is the US secret intelligence service

explanation.surface: An amateur spy is caught by an intelligence agency, perhaps with a planted mole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a spy placed undercover, but it is just a living plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The acacia is a tree or shrub, the wattle, so it is a member of the plant kingdom.

clue.text: Complaint from 12 who ran with 2 inveighing against 5 leadership

indicators.note: leadership points to the leading letters, so only the first of each word is kept

blocks.note: Sebastian Coe, Olympic middle-distance runner and later a Tory MP
L is the abbreviation for Liberal, the answer to the cross-referenced clue
first letters of inveighing, against and Corbyn, the cross-referenced answer

explanation.surface: A political grievance from a Tory who stood with the Liberals, railing at Corbyn's leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross-references: 12 is TORY, 2 is LIBERAL, 5 is CORBYN. Coe ran in the Olympics, not just for Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Coeliac disease is a digestive disorder triggered by gluten, and complaint is a common word for an illness.

clue.text: Beloved party embraced by American lefty

indicators.note: something embraced is held in another's arms, so it sits within the other letters

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
a do is an informal party
a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A beloved political party is welcomed by an American left-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beloved is dearly loved, so adored, used as an adjective, means the same.

clue.text: Magic practitioner has wife turned into large reptile

indicators.note: turned into means changed to, so one letter is replaced by another

blocks.note: a wizard practises magic
W is the abbreviation for wife
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A sorcerer turns his wife into a big reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large reptile' reads as one phrase, but 'large' is the replacement letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lizard is a scaly four-legged reptile such as a gecko or iguana.

clue.text: Platform with exotic hyacinths, last three plucked for floral decoration

indicators.note: plucking pulls things away, so the final three letters are removed
exotic means strange or foreign, so these letters take on an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: a dais is a raised platform
taken as written, then trimmed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A stage is decked with unusual hyacinths, some of their blooms picked off for a floral display.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy chain is a string of daisies threaded together by their stems, worn as a garland.

clue.text: I headed back to arrive at food store

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the words are read right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
to head a group is to lead it

explanation.surface: Someone describes heading home to reach a food shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared food.

clue.text: Hairy fellow's reportedly the guy spotted in the East End

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, and the East End accent drops its h sounds

blocks.clueFragment: the guy spotted in the East End
blocks.note: a Cockney says 'he saw' without the h, and the guy spotted is he who saw

explanation.surface: A hairy man is said to have been seen in East London.
explanation.walkthrough: East End Cockneys traditionally drop initial h. In Genesis, Jacob says his brother is a hairy man.
explanation.definitionFit: Esau, Jacob's twin in Genesis, was born covered in red hair, the Bible's famous hairy man.

clue.text: Portion of film about British maverick

indicators.note: about means around, so the film portion surrounds the other letter

blocks.note: a reel is a spool or section of cinema film
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A fragment of film tells the story of a British nonconformist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Portion of film' looks like it might hide letters inside a word, but it is a reel.
explanation.definitionFit: A maverick is an independent-minded person who defies convention, much like a rebel.

clue.text: Economist who creates barriers?

blocks.note: surface reading: a protectionist economist who puts up trade barriers
setter's reading: a smith is a maker, as a wordsmith makes words, so think of a maker of river barriers, preceded by the indefinite article

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests tariffs; really it splits the famous name as 'a dam-smith', someone who makes dams, as a wordsmith makes words. Adam Smith wrote The Wealth of Nations and championed free trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam Smith, the eighteenth-century Scottish thinker, is the founding figure of classical political economy.

clue.text: Drum musician in club with brief set

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: a DJ, disc jockey, plays music in a nightclub
to embed is to set something firmly in place

explanation.surface: A drummer plays a short set in a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' reads as a musical performance, but it is a verb meaning fix in place.
explanation.definitionFit: The djembe is a goblet-shaped hand drum from West Africa, played with bare hands.

clue.text: Evening wear, about to be carried separately by relatives' subordinates

indicators.note: carried by means held inside, and separately means two items go in at different points

blocks.note: aunts are relatives
DJ is a dinner jacket, formal evening wear
c is circa, Latin for about, used with dates

explanation.surface: Junior staff carry their relatives' evening clothes for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjuncts are assistants or secondary things attached to something more important, so they are subordinates.
